doc.title: Steve Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 25, 2002

title: The Passages record and bringing in all influences
summary: Passages combines jazz, R&B, funk, Kool and the Gang and avant garde influences.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: that bounce. So certainly yeah, that’s a part of it. And particularly in “Q-B-Rab,” there’s a lot of elements that I was addressing. And even the record, the whole recording, “Passages,” which is the title of that, the purpose I guess that I had in mind was to bring together all of the influences that I’ve had as a musician and growing up and hearing all of these different kinds of music and jazz and R&B and funk, avante garde, within the thread of that tune you know you can find Eddie Harris, Ornette Coleman, you know, second line, Kool and the Gang, there’s a figure in there right out of Kool and the Gang, “Hollywood Swinging” [scats].

And that’s what it is. And by the way in their pre-Kool and the Gang life they were a jazz group. And so I was very influenced by them, particularly Ronald Bell, who was heavily influenced by John Coltrane. So the music to me is all this incredible tapestry with these different threads. Or we could think about it with an amazing tree with all of these branches. And it’s all music, it’s all a continuum. And I try not to so much in my own music, try not to say well we can’t allow ourselves to think this way because we’re thinking that way. We all are who we are because of what we grew up with. We were all fed on different things, artistically and just as human beings. So I think the artist, being true to oneself brings all of that in. You know you can’t deny who you are. You are who you are. So bring it all in there. That’s what it’s all about. That’s what art is all about. Honesty. So bring it all in. And that’s what I feel we were able to accomplish with this record.
